subject: Proposal: Renewal term anchoring + capacity uptick (Aperture Labs)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Lina Torres <lina.torres@aperture.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal proposal: term anchoring + capacity uptick (Aperture Labs)

Hi Lina —

Thanks again for the time last week. As discussed, I put together a pragmatic renewal path that keeps your unit economics predictable while enabling the throughput uplift you flagged for Q3. High-level proposal: 

- Term: 12 months (renewal effective 2027-04-01)
- Commitment: 40% increase over current committed tokens (stepped cadence: 10% extra in months 1-3, 15% months 4-8, remainder thereafter)
- Commercials: 20% list discount on the committed tier (applies to committed usage)
- Price hold: 90 days from countersign (to allow for procurement/PO)
- Onboarding credit: $25,000 one-time credit to cover migration engineering + model tuning sessions

I attached a revised SOW and a pricing sheet that shows the blended cost impact and a scenario with a higher commit. If Aperture is ready to lock the increase we can translate this into an amendment + DocuSign and push the PO through. 

Would you be available for a 30-minute sync tomorrow to walk the numbers with procurement? If procurement has a target price or a required price-hold window, call it out and we’ll try to accommodate.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: Aperture_SOW_v3.pdf, redwood_pricing_sheet_v2.xlsx
From: Lina Torres <lina.torres@aperture.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 15:40:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal: term anchoring + capacity uptick (Aperture Labs)

Ben —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear scenarios. A few notes from procurement and finance: 

1) Price hold: we need 180 days minimum to finalize internal approvals and align with our quarter close. 90 days will be tight.
2) Discount: Aperture is also evaluating a competing provider; procurement has asked whether you can move the committed discount to 25% for the first 12 months to match their pricing band.
3) Credits: the $25k onboarding credit is helpful but not sufficient to cover the tuning work our ML infra team anticipates. If you can increase to $50k we can avoid a separate service PO.
4) Contract: we’ll also need any changes to data residency and audit log retention noted in the amendment — that’s a separate thread but should be reflected.

Can you share an updated mark that reflects a 180-day hold, a 25% first-year committed discount, and $50k in credits? Procurement would like that as a single-line commercial position we can present to legal.

Thanks,
Lina
Lina Torres
Head of Procurement, Aperture Labs
lina.torres@aperture.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:05:18 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal proposal: Aperture asks (25% / 180d / $50k credit)

Team — forwarding Aperture's asks. Quick summary: they want 180-day price hold, 25% committed discount Y1, and $50k onboarding credit. Procurement is explicit about competitive pressure.

Options I see: 
- Option A (conservative): Approve 22% committed discount + $35k credit + 180d hold — we retain 3% margin and limit credit exposure.
- Option B (more aggressive): Approve 25% discount + $50k credit + 180d hold in exchange for an explicit 18-month minimum term and a stepped commit guarantee (the 40% uptick locked in by Q4).
- Option C (counter-offer): Keep 20% discount, extend price hold to 180d, increase credit to $40k, and add a 6-month ramp SLA that gives us runway to manage burst.

I attached internal pricing_scenarios for modeling. Aperture is strategic in retail — upsell potential across two more product lines in H2 if we can win this renewal. If we lose on price there’s a high chance they go into a bake-off.

Can you advise which option we should present? If we pick B I’ll ask legal to prep the 18-month amendment and we’ll route for approval.

Thanks,
Ben
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Lina Torres <lina.torres@aperture.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Renewal proposal: term anchoring + capacity uptick (Aperture Labs)

Hi Lina —

Thanks for the transparency and for outlining procurement’s priorities. Aperture is an important partner and we want to make a commercially defensible offer that keeps the door open for the wider expansion you referenced. After internal review we can do the following: 

- Commitment & term: 18-month amendment starting 2027-04-01 with the 40% commit uplift (stepped cadence as proposed).
- Discount: 22% off list on the committed tier for the first 12 months, reverting to 16% for the remainder of the term.
- Price hold: 180 days from countersign on the committed tier pricing.
- Onboarding credit: $40,000 one-time credit to cover migration support and tuning sessions.
- Other: we will reflect data residency confirmations and audit-log retention in the amendment; legal will draft the clause.

Next steps: I’ve attached a revised SOW and a clean pricing sheet reflecting these numbers. If that direction is acceptable, I’ll circulate the amendment for countersign and send a DocuSign link. Aperture PO timeline permitting we can target an April 1 start.

If you’d like to approve a different split (e.g., flat 25% for 12 months) I can escalate to revenue ops, but the concession above is what we can approve without executive sign-off.

Would you like a 20–30 minute handoff with Soojin and Marissa to get legal/ops prepped?

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Aperture_SOW_v3.pdf (revised), redwood_pricing_sheet_v2.xlsx (final)
